To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aurein  2.5, an antimicrobial peptide, kills yeasts via a membranolytic mechanism and may be a useful template for the development antifungal agents.
aurein 1.2 and 2.5 are highly active against the fungal strains R. rubra and S. pombe, and that the mechanism of action involves membrane perturbation and lysis.
Aurein 2. 5 is a novel peptide antibiotic that kills yeasts via membrane-interactive mechanisms and may be used as a template for developing antifungal agents with novel modes of action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antimicrobial properties of aurein 1.2, a peptide antibiotic produced by Australian tree frogs (Litoria aurea).
the development of novel antimicrobial agents, and in this paper we report on the activity of aurein-2.5 against the yeast strains: Rhodoturula rubra and Shizosaccharomces pombe.
the antimicrobial activities of a group of naturally occurring cationic antimicrobial peptides, the aureins, against a wide range of bacterial, fungal and viral pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aurein 1.2, 1.5 and 2.5 peptides have been reported to have antifungal activity against Candida albicans and Rhodotorula mucilaginosa.
aurein 1.2 and aurein 2-5 have a potential to be developed as antifungal agents against the yeasts R. rubra and S. pombe.
Aurein 2.4 is an effective antimicrobial peptide against a variety of microorganisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aurein 1.5, aurein 1-2, aurein 2, aurein 2.2, aurein2.5, aurelin 2.6, aurein 3, aurein 4.1, aurein 5, aurein 5.2, aureinin 1.2, and aureinin 2 are all active against yeasts.

aurein 1.2, aurein 2, aurein 1.5 and aurein 2A, aurein 1B and 1C, and aurein 1D and 2.5 have similar membrane-interactive α-structures and similar membrane-penetrating and membrane-disrupting activities.
aurein 1.2, aurein 2 and aurein 2A are all able to kill yeasts via membranolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aureins, a family of antimicrobial peptides isolated from the skin of Australian frogs, are active against a broad range of microorganisms and may be useful as a template for designing novel antifungal agents.
aurein 1.2 is a promising candidate for the development of new antimicrobial peptides against fungal pathogens.
aurein  2.5 may serve as a lead compound for the development of novel antifungals with a novel mechanism of action.
